scope: static review; no received code executed

findings.title: Validate output duration before accepting the timing result
findings.body: The output timing check only rejects falsy values. With source_rows equal to [{"pts": 0, "duration": 0.063}] and output_duration equal to -0.1, the duration is truthy and passes the comparison against -0.187, producing an accepted verdict for an impossible negative audio duration. A positive infinite duration also passes for any finite source span; Python's JSON decoder can produce this from the JSON numeric literal 1e309. expected_result forwards the decoded output_audio_duration directly to this checker, and verify_result recomputes the same verdict, so pin and result verification do not correct it. Require a finite, positive numeric output duration before applying the shortening tolerance, and cover invalid output timing in the checker tests.

limitations: Only the packaged public source snapshot was inspected; no other files, memory, credentials, keys, or network sources were accessed.
No received code, imports, tests, signing commands, or Casita commands were executed; the finding is based on static control flow and arithmetic.
The review covered authentication.py, handoff.py, demo.py, the trusted fixture checker, their packaged tests, fixture observations, and capsule metadata.
The packaged authentication tests import signed_handoff, but that implementation is absent from the capsule, so its orchestration and cleanup behavior could not be reviewed.
Casita implementation and runtime behavior, OpenSSH implementation, external configuration, and deployment context were unavailable.
The packaged fixture observations use finite positive output durations; the finding concerns other observation values accepted by the same checker path.
This static review does not establish execution provenance, sandboxing, signature validity, or exhaustive absence of defects.
